newsitem.title: BULGARIA: GREECE'S INTRACOM TO DEVELOP BULGARIAN LOTTERY.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S INTRACOM TO DEVELOP BULGARIAN LOTTERY.

text.p: Greece's Intracom group plans to develop Bulgaria's sports lottery and sharply increase its profits by implementing modern automatic systems, its managing director said on Friday.

"Under the contract Intracom will supply, install and develop a complete information system aimed at the automation of the current games and those the lottery will choose in the future," Pericles Katsioulas told Reuters in an interview.
Intracom and its daughter firm Intralot sealed a 12-year deal with the Bulgarian sports lottery operator on September 16 and the Greek grouping will invest more than $40 million.

"This is the biggest investment in the field of information technology and electronics in Bulgaria since 1990 and also the greatest foreign investment in the country in recent months after a severe economic crisis has occurred," Katsioulas said.
The contract sparked a row in Bulgaria amid fears that the Greek group would privatise or syphon off lottery profits.
Bulgaria's chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev said the contract was "shameful" and that he wanted to see it to assess whether the law had been broken.
Katsioulas said there had not been a single ambiguous item in "this normal international contract" involving a supplier of equipment and services and a buyer.
"There is not a hint of any hidden privatisation," he said, adding that the main criticism of the contract came from commercial rivals.
Under the contract Intracom will not implement a decision of the International Arbitrage Court in Paris, Katsioulas said.
Last year the Paris court ruled that the Bulgarian lottery should pay Intracom a total of $10 million including interest as compensation for cancelling an earlier contract in 1993.
A Bulgarian court is expected to rule on the Paris court decision next week.
"It is stated clearly in the contract that Intracom will not seek this money. We went to Paris because we had an agreement which was cancelled unilaterally," Katsioulas said.
Intracom will receive five percent of the lottery's annual revenues plus 10 percent of the additional increased revenues, which guarantees that Intracom will seek a rise in sales.

The project for the modernisation of the lottery envisages the construction of 6,000 terminals linked with 25 centres. On-Line systems will be installed and the regional centres will be connected to the national one through a V-SAT satelite.
The whole system will be completed in three years, while part of it will start operating in June 1997.

"The Bulgarian sports totalisator will become the owner of the whole system and will have all the rights over the games and will receive and manage all the revenues," Katsioulas said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569; 981 4145
